Ledn co-founder Mauricio Di Bartolomeo calls rising borrowing costs a rounding error next to $BTC's upside, with even the smallest Ledn loans cheaper than Strategy's 12% preferreds

"The cost of borrowing against your stocks just went up by 25 bps. How much are stocks up by this year?"

"The increase of the debt of the carrying costs has become a rounding error compared to the upside of the underlying position that loan is financing. It's similar to the dynamic we see with Bitcoin-backed loans."

"A Bitcoin-backed loan interest rate at Ledn starts at 9.25%. Anybody that took a loan from Ledn at 9.25% when Bitcoin was at 65 or 70 has seen the value of that collateral increase by 25 to 35%."

"As long as the cost of financing the debt is a fraction of the price action of the asset that debt is financing, we're still very much in the clear in terms of those ratios and that dynamic."

"Every single person at Ledn today, even at a $500 loan, can borrow at lower interest than what Strategy's paying on their preferreds. The smallest loan at Ledn is 11.49%. STRC yields are at 12% right now."

posts.text:
Ledn co-founder Mauricio Di Bartolomeo on how tokenized gold gives anyone access to Swiss-vaulted gold, free of country-level risks

"Gold is one of those things that even though it's the same asset, it's not treated the same based on where it is."

"If you tell somebody you have a million dollars worth of gold in a vault in Switzerland, they react very differently than you say you have a million dollars worth of gold in a vault in Venezuela or in Zimbabwe."

"How much can I borrow with my gold that's in Venezuela? The answer will be zero. Or you would have to basically find a person comfortable with lending you anything using Venezuelan gold as collateral."

"Because different countries have different property rights, different regulatory risks, different corruption regimes."

"Tokenized gold addresses this problem, which is to say, let's keep the gold in the highest quality vaults in a very high quality property rights government like the Swiss government in a Swiss vault, the highest of standards, and let's give everybody a token receipt of the gold in that vault."

posts.name: Trung Phan
posts.text:
Really enjoyed You Can See Everything. Might be most meta documentary ever.  

No spoilers but will say this interview Christopher Nolan did with Nathan Fielder about his show “The Curse” — explaining his creative process — really comes through in Holmes film:

▫️setting the tone is his top priority, even moreso than narrative (“when you have the tone right, everything falls into place”) 

▫️Fielder says he “stumbles into ideas he gets excited about” without a master plan and “just piles things on and it grows” (for the Holmes doc, he had an agreement with A24 to scrap the project even after years of shooting if he didn’t think there was a film)

▫️the musical score is crucial in setting the tone (the sound doesn’t even have to match action on the scene, it can float above just setting mood)

▫️he doesn’t want to rush scenes; let them develop to the point where audience is expecting any action to be consequential and it builds the tension (inspired by old detective TV show Columbo)

***

Full interview here (Nolan really is a Fielder Stan): https://youtu.be/etoG2I6gaHE?si=SPNzDV9H5O5NG90S

posts.text:
Saw some comments about my post on this topic 👇 🤣 

1. I am always supportive of any blockchain making any progress in any country. BTC, ETH, BNB, XRP, SOL, HYPE, ZEC, SIGN, all stablecoins, etc, you name it...

2. I was happy that SOL can advertise and get an office in Shanghai. It would open the path for others to follow. It would also indicate that "China unbanned crypto", which would be positive news for all of us. But alas, that's not quite the case yet, it seems...

3. My X post was not the trigger. It's now emerged that the Bund building ad was taken down within 10 minutes. (If you don't know, China monitors speech and media in real-time.) I only saw it on X 12-24 hours after the fact. 

4. Regardless of the outcome, it's good effort. Keep building and keep pushing adoption.

quoted.text:
Solana just had its event in China shut down.

And the funniest part is that CZ basically warned about this one day earlier.

First Solana Foundation announced that it has opened an office in Pudong, occupying one of the highest commercial office spaces

All of this in a country where crypto is heavily restricted.

A day before CZ notices Solana’s expansion and publicly comments on how surprising it is.

He says it’s amazing that Solana can advertise and open an office in China.

(Especially considering BNB Chain hasn’t been able to do the same)

Sounds pretty reasonable, right?

Well, less than 24 hours later…

The first event was supposed to take place at the Shangri-La hotel in Shanghai.

The event was scheduled to begin at 10 AM.

Instead, attendees arrived to find police officers at the venue.

You genuinely cannot make this stuff up.

Around noon, organizers sent an apology email arguing “Venue logistics considerations.”

CZ them posted:

“Sad to see. Looks like they really didn’t know the local policies?”

And reminded everyone that something similar had happened less than a year ago.

I’ve seen people joking that he snitched on them.

I actually respect Solana’s ambition to expand into one of the biggest markets

But I think there’s a difference between building blockchain infrastructure in China and publicly promoting a crypto ecosystem

This week Solana might have crossed that line and CZ is probably thinking he told them so.
